page: OVHcloud c3-64 is a compute-optimized server instance built on the KVM hypervisor and x86_64 architecture. It features 32 dedicated physical cores and 32 vCPUs powered by an AMD EPYC processor running at 2.3 GHz. The CPU configuration operates with one thread per core, meaning hyperthreading is disabled. Memory capacity is 64.0 GB, yielding a resource density of 2.0 GB of RAM per core. Storage is provided by a local 400 GB NVMe SSD, and the network interface delivers a baseline bandwidth of 4 Gbps.

In benchmark evaluations, the instance demonstrates strong multi-core and single-core CPU performance, placing in the top 25% for stress-ng and Passmark CPU tests. Memory performance is particularly notable, with the Passmark memory score reaching the top 10% tier, supported by strong read and write memory bandwidth across both cached and uncached large-block tests. For data processing, bzip3 multi-threaded decompression and Redis SET operations both rank in the top 25%, while single-threaded gzip compression and static web serving throughput perform in the middle 50% average tier.

The server's hardware profile presents a clear tradeoff: while it offers high compute density with dedicated physical cores and top-tier memory performance, the 2.0 GB RAM-per-core ratio limits its suitability for memory-intensive datasets. It is optimized for compute-heavy workloads, multi-threaded data decompression, database operations, and small-to-medium scale language model inference, where its strong prompt processing and text generation speeds for 135M models can be fully utilized.
